title: How green is your money?
reason: 上一课关注拖延与任务管理，今天轮换到金融经济与消费决策。本集讨论银行如何使用客户资金、可持续投资、信息透明度和漂绿风险，贴近金融科技中的资金流向展示、产品披露与客户选择。练习通过重复调用常见搭配和因果表达，训练用简单英语说明资金用途、判断依据和改进建议。

targetExpressions.meaning: make careful and sensible choices about something
targetExpressions.usage: Use it before a noun or -ing form: Customers should be smart about choosing financial products.
Use it to make a strong contrast: Some business practices are far from environmentally friendly.

targetExpressions.meaning: join a popular activity mainly because it seems likely to succeed
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when motives may be based on popularity: Some companies jump on the bandwagon without making real changes.

targetExpressions.meaning: move your money to another bank, business or provider
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when a customer chooses a competitor: If the fees stay high, customers may take their money elsewhere.

targetExpressions.meaning: be open and honest about something without hiding important information
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for clear disclosure: Banks should be transparent about how customer deposits are used.

targetExpressions.meaning: focus attention on something, often to reveal a problem
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when scrutiny increases: The report put the spotlight on unclear investment rules.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the programme's advice: One effective action is to ______ investing your money.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil says one of the most effective things people can do is be smart about investing their money.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the contrast: Some businesses funded by bank deposits are ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript says customers' money funds businesses, some of which are far from environmentally friendly.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does “jump on the bandwagon” suggest about a bank's reason for offering a green product?

options.text: It may be following a popular trend rather than showing genuine commitment.
It has stopped offering all investment products.
It has made its accounting completely secret.
It is the first organisation to consider the environment.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme defines the idiom as joining an activity because it is popular and likely to succeed, not because of real interest.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the customer action from the transcript: Banks may change when customers threaten to ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Beth says banks rely on customers' money and may change their behaviour when customers threaten to take their money elsewhere.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: If a bank is “transparent about” its investments, what should customers be able to do?

options.text: See and understand clearly how the money is invested.
Receive a guaranteed return from every investment.
Keep the investment strategy hidden from competitors and customers.
Avoid making any choices about their pension.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript explains that transparent means open and honest, so it is easy to see and understand how a business works.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the phrase: Greater public interest can ______ how pension funds are being used.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil says customer demand puts the spotlight on how pension funds are used, including whether they support oil or renewable energy.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why is “jumping on the bandwagon” connected with concern about greenwashing?

options.text: A company may market itself as green because the idea is popular without making serious environmental changes.
A company may refuse to mention environmental issues in any advertisement.
A company may invest only in small specialised funds.
A company may ask customers to stop using bank accounts.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Greenwashing means appearing environmentally friendly without serious action; joining a popular trend for advantage can produce that gap.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: According to the programme, changing your pension may be how many times more effective than avoiding meat and flying combined?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil says changing a pension is thought to be twenty-one times more effective than avoiding meat and stopping flying put together.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) money flow—what banks do with customer money; (2) problem—greenwashing and unclear motives; (3) response—how customer demand can increase transparency. Phrase bank: “jump on the bandwagon”, “be transparent about”, “put the spotlight on”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough.
referencePoints: Money kept in a bank is invested to fund other businesses, including some that are not environmentally friendly.
Ethical banking used to be a niche interest but has become much more widely discussed.
Some businesses may jump on the environmental bandwagon or use greenwashing without making serious changes.
Banks rely on customer money and may respond when customers threaten to move it elsewhere.
More demand for responsible pensions can make companies more transparent and draw attention to how funds are used.
The programme says changing a pension may have a much larger climate impact than avoiding meat and flying together.
